chapter_title: Concerning the Four Great Days that have come forth from one another, together with the Four Nights
chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is dominant. A four-fold day/night schema maps cosmic entities to twelve-hour structures. The substrate is clean through the first three positions of each sequence. The fourth positions (day 4 = Jesus the Splendour, night 4 = law of Sin) show editorial bridging toward institutional identifications ('his church,' 'the twelve sects,' 'the old man'). This is a classic pattern: the editor extends a complete cosmic schema into the contemporary world at the terminal position. The substrate pentadic structure (five elements, five sense organs, five spirits) underlies the twelve-fold systematization, which Gardner rightly notes is 'secondary' — yet the cosmic correspondences within each position (zodiacal signs as Matter's thrones, five parts above/below, heat and cold as father and mother) are genuinely substratic. Editorial fatigue is moderate: substrate vocabulary drops from 34.09 to 8.62 in the second half while editorial_bridge rises from 0.0 to 2.39.

paragraphs.core_text: Four great days have come forth from one another; they were evoked out of one another!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again the enlightener speaks:' — dialogue frame attribution formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Standard dialogue frame opening wrapping a substantive cosmological declaration. The teaching statement defines the schema (four days, evoked from one another) and belongs to the oldest layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The first great day is the Father, the God of truth, the fir[st ... ... m]idst the aeons of his greatness, in his [l]iving kingdom. The twelve hours of this great day are the twelve great rich Gods of greatness. These, who are the first evocations that he evoked (to mirror) his greatness, he spread out to the four climes, three by three before his face.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure degree-mapping: first day → Father → twelve hours → twelve rich Gods → four climes (3×4=12). 'Evocations that he evoked' is characteristic substrate emanation vocabulary. The spatial distribution 'three by three before his face' is systematic cosmological architecture. All mappings stay within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The second day is the Third Ambassador, the one who dwells in the light ship. His twelve hours are the twelve virgins that he evoked in his greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very high substrate density (75.0). Clean degree-mapping: second day → Third Ambassador → light ship (cosmic geography) → twelve virgins. 'Evoked in his greatness' repeats the emanation formula from ¶2.

paragraphs.core_text: [The third day is the Pillar of Glory, the great porter that is greater than] all [the po]rters; the one that supports all [ ... ], those above and those below. Its twelve hours are the five sons of the First Man; the five sons of the Living Spirit, who support all the weights of the universe; together with the summons and the obedience, which are counted to their ten brethren. These are the twelve light hours of the third day.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily restored opening (brackets) but pattern is clear: third day → Pillar of Glory → twelve hours composed of two pentads + a dyad (5+5+2=12). The summation formula 'These are the twelve light hours of the third day' closes the teaching unit. The pentadic sub-structure (five sons × 2) reflects the substrate's native five-fold organization being fitted into the twelve-fold schema.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth day is Jesus the Splendour. His twelve hours are the twelve wisdoms, which are his [light] h[o]u[rs].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'who [dwells in] his church' — institutional identification. The parallel cosmic entities dwell in cosmic locations (living kingdom ¶2, light ship ¶3) while 'his church' reaches toward the institutional Manichaean community. The fourth position in this schema is consistently where editorial bridging occurs (cf. fourth night ¶14-15).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Institutional vocabulary fires (20.83). The pattern demands a locating clause for the fourth entity; the substrate likely had a cosmic location that was replaced with 'his church.' The twelve wisdoms as hours is substratic — purely cosmic mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the four great days that have come forth from one another, which were evoked out of one another.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'They [ ... Blessed is] every one who will know them, and [ ... ] the light!' — beatitude/exhortation closure formula. 'Blessed is every one who will know them' is the standard exhortation pattern that the compilers appended to substrate teaching sequences.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The summary statement ('These are the four great days...') is a substrate closure paralleling ¶16 for the nights. The beatitude is standard devotional wrapper. The bridge connective flag ('These are the') is a false positive — this is a demonstrative summary, not an editorial seam.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.26⟩ [ ... ]: For just as four day[s ex]ist, s[o] too four nights exist.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Transitional teaching statement linking the two halves of the schema. The lacuna with colon '[ ... ]:' likely contained a dialogue attribution, but since it is unreadable, the visible text is preserved as substrate. The structural parallel (four days → four nights) is the teaching's own architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: The first night is the land of Darkness. It has twelve black [shadows] therein, which are its dark h[o]ur[s]. The twelve shadows of the first night are the five elements of the land of Darkness, [which] poured forth from its five sense organs; and [ ... ] which [ ... ] in its [fi]ve elements and its five [ ... ]; the five [sp]irits that dwell in its elements [ ... ]. These are the twelve shadows and spirits of the first night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Perfect substrate pattern: first night → land of Darkness → twelve shadows composed of pentadic sub-structures (five elements + five sense organs + five spirits? — damaged but structure is clear). 'Poured forth from its five sense organs' is cosmic emanation vocabulary. The pentadic architecture mirrors the day sequence.

paragraphs.core_text: The second night is Matter, the sculptress [ ... ... ] who has sculpted [ ... ] and the entire ruling-power that is in the worl[ds of Darkness]. She has fashioned it in five sense organs, five [male] and five female, two per world; together with the fire and the lust [that] dwell in men and women, inflaming [them] inward to one another. These are the twelve spirits of this second night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Matter as 'sculptress' is a cosmic agent designation — describes what she IS and does within the system. The five-fold gender pairing (five male, five female, 'two per world') is systematic cosmological architecture. 'Fire and lust dwelling in men and women' stays within the cosmic body-system — describes cosmic forces operating in the body-cosmos, not contemporary moral application.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed she, this Matter, the thought of death, ga[ve] the King of the realms of Darkness and his powers strength for the war and the fight, against the aeons of greatness. Yet, he was caught! They laid a snare for him through the Fi[rst M]an. [He] was ta[ken] t[o ... ] through the powers [ ... He] was brought up from the land of death and s[et ... ab]ove and below in the [whole] universe; in the five par[t]s in the heavens above, as well as the five [parts] in the earths below; together with the heat and the cold that are the father and the mother, their fire and their l[u]st.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic narrative: the war, the First Man as snare, the five-fold distribution above and below. 'The heat and the cold that are the father and the mother' is a cosmic correspondence — thermal polarity mapped to generative polarity. All mappings stay within the cosmic system. Low substrate score (10.71) is because the vocabulary is narrative rather than terminological, but the content is entirely cosmic-to-cosmic.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the second night that is begotten from the first night. They laid a snare for her through the First M[a]n. She was brought up by the hand of the Living Spirit, and set in this composite univers[e ... ] he[r], above and below. The [upper side is the sense] organs of males; the lower side [ ... ] fe[mal]es.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the cosmic narrative of the second night. 'Begotten from the first night' echoes the schema's evocation-from-one-another principle. The upper/lower mapping to male/female sense organs is body-cosmos correspondence. 'Composite universe' is substrate cosmological terminology.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.27⟩ The thir[d night is the five] worlds of flesh [ ... five] male, and five female; that were begotten from the powers [abo]ve. They have fallen upon the earth, being displayed in wh[at is d]ry and what is moist; together with the fire and the lust [that d]we[l]l in them, which drives them inward to one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third night → five worlds of flesh. Five male/five female continues the pentadic gender-pairing of ¶9. 'Dry and moist' is an elemental polarity mapping. 'Fire and lust driving them inward to one another' repeats the cosmic force description from ¶9 — systematic correspondence, not moral application.

paragraphs.core_text: [Mat]te[r] herself, the thought of death, is the [mother] of them all; as among them she is named 'the night'. [The worlds] of male and female fleshes, together with the fire and the l[ust], shall [ ... ] twelve hours of [ ... ... ] night. Again, [it] too, the third night that is in the worlds of fl[e]sh, was begotten from the second night; which the Living [Spir]it crucified in the uni[verse ... , ab]ove and below in heaven [ ... ... ].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Matter as 'the night' is a cosmic identity mapping — she IS the principle of darkness. 'Mother of them all' maps Matter's generative role in the cosmic system. 'The Living Spirit crucified in the universe' is cosmic process vocabulary — not a Christological reference but a description of how Matter was bound in the cosmic structure. Heavy lacunae but the teaching skeleton is visible.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth night is the law of Sin, which is the dark spirit who speaks in the twelve spirits. They are the nakednesses, the twelve zodiacal signs of Matter. They are her thrones.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'the twelve sects' — editorial bridge identifying the twelve spirits with contemporary religious groups (one side of the mapping leaves the cosmic system). Removed 'she who is made public, as she sculpts and is displayed in the old man' — editorial bridge connecting cosmic Matter to the Pauline 'old man' concept. 'Sculpts' is substrate vocabulary (cf. ¶9 'sculptress') but here it serves the editorial identification with the old man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Editorial_bridge score peaks at 15.69. The substrate core maps fourth night → law of Sin → twelve spirits → zodiacal signs → Matter's thrones. This is cosmic-to-cosmic (spirits → zodiac → Matter). The editorial layer then identifies these spirits with 'the twelve sects' and Matter's display with 'the old man' — both reaching into the contemporary religious world. The seam falls after 'her thrones.'

paragraphs.core_text: the hours of this fourth night are the twelve e[vi]l spirits; the [ ... ] which [are ... ... ... ... di]fferentiate the day and night [ ... ... of] death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'And, also,' (bridge connective). Removed 'that is the old man, who reigns in the sects' — editorial bridge identifying the fourth night with the Pauline old man and contemporary sects. Removed 'of the old man' — second occurrence of editorial identification embedded in the substrate structure.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Editorial_bridge at 10.64, institutional at 4.26. The substrate element (twelve evil spirits as hours, differentiating day and night) follows the pattern of ¶¶8-9. The editorial additions ('the old man,' 'the sects') are syntactically inserted into the substrate frame as appositives and possessives. Heavy lacunae make precise extraction difficult.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the fourth night [ ... ] that have come forth of one another. One has [ ... ... ] just like the days of lig[ht ... ] they manifested one another. So als[o ... ] they did arise out of one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate summary/closure paralleling ¶6 for the days. Despite heavy lacunae, the surviving text restates the schema's foundational principle: arising out of one another, manifesting one another. All vocabulary scores at 0.0 — no editorial layer vocabulary detected. The 'just like the days of light' explicitly links the night closure to the day sequence.

'Blessed is he who will know them, and separate them' — standard beatitude/devotional closure formula. Matches the exhortation pattern identified across the corpus. 'Separate them' may reflect the teaching's content (separating days from nights, light from darkness) but the vehicle is the compilers' devotional wrapper, not the substrate's systematic voice.
